title: Word 21 — On the Threats of God
attribution_note: Word 21 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: The King's Law and Its Penalties

pairs.en: We see the threats written in Holy Scripture, by which God warns unrepentant sinners of temporal and eternal punishment. For just as a king who cares for the good order of his realm issues a beneficial decree, declaring in it what his subjects must and must not do, and appointing in the same decree a penalty for lawbreakers — saying, “such and such shall befall the one who transgresses this decree” — so too the Heavenly King, the Lord God, has given His holy and righteous law to all people, that they might live by the rule of this law and amend themselves, turning away from what He forbids and doing what He commands. And to those who transgress the law He has declared temporal and eternal punishment: *“Even now the axe is laid to the root of the trees: every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire”* [Matthew 3:10]. *“But the fearful, and unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and whoremongers, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and brimstone: which is the second death”* [Revelation 21:8]. *“If he turn not, he will sharpen his sword; he has bent his bow, and made it ready.* *He has also prepared for him the instruments of death; he ordains his arrows against the persecutors”* [Psalm 7:13–14]. *“Upon the wicked he shall rain snares, fire and brimstone, and a horrible tempest: this shall be the portion of their cup”* [Psalm 10:6/11:6]. *“Be not deceived: neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor the effeminate, nor abusers of themselves with mankind, nor thieves, nor covetous, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor extortioners, shall inherit the kingdom of God”* [1 Corinthians 6:9–10].

sections.heading: Why God Warns Us: An Act of Love

pairs.en: These and other threats of God are fearful to us, yet they show us God's great love for mankind. For nothing turns a sinner to repentance so surely as the threat of punishment. Through the promise of blessings God calls us to Himself and to eternal salvation, but through the threat of punishment He urges, compels, and persuades us. He warns sinners precisely because He does not wish to destroy them. He shows forth His wrath so that, through fear of that wrath, we might amend ourselves and escape eternal punishment. For if fear of an earthly king turns us away from much evil, how much more is fear of the Heavenly King able to turn us from every evil and move us to repentance, if we often ponder His righteous anger against sin and His fearful threats.

Truly, by fear of punishment a man will be bound and restrained as if by a rope, and will not be moved to any evil. Truly he will not wish to sin when, before the eyes of his mind, he beholds the eternal fire prepared for his sin. Truly the remembrance of punishment will keep him from the punishment, and reflection on hell will keep him from entering hell. Truly we owe our God a great debt, beloved Christians, for this very love of His toward us — that He has warned us of hell and of the other punishments. For, as was said above, the threat of punishment moves us to repentance more than the promise of blessings.

sections.heading: The Peril of Despising God's Warnings

pairs.en: But open the hearing of your souls and attend to what I wish to set before you. It is dangerous, exceedingly dangerous, to despise God's threats, and not repent, and not amend oneself. Know for certain, and do not doubt, that whoever despises His threats will in truth come to know God's punishment upon himself. There is nothing more perilous than to despise what God threatens. He who does not think of hell will fall into hell. He who despises eternal death will not escape it. He who does not fear the wrath of God, and does not repent, will come to know that wrath upon himself. *“Our God is a consuming fire.* *It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God”* [Hebrews 10:31]! *“God is not mocked”* [Galatians 6:7]. Whatever a man sows, that he will also reap. God is indeed merciful and loves mankind, but He is also righteous, for He will render to everyone according to his deeds.

sections.heading: Examples from Scripture: None Who Despised Escaped

pairs.en: Our first parents despised this, and died. The ungodly who lived in the days of Noah despised the threats of God, and perished in the universal flood. The Sodomites despised them, and were burned with fire. Sinners despise them even now, and perish. The ungodly who did not believe righteous Noah's preaching of repentance were drowned in the flood. What, then, should today's ungodly, scoffers, and despisers of God's law expect? They too will be swallowed up in the most terrible flood of eternal destruction. Fire from heaven burned the Sodomites for their vile impurity. What should today's fornicators, adulterers, and other defilers look for, but the fire of hell, in which they will burn and not be consumed forever? Many Israelites were struck down in the wilderness for their transgressions and did not reach the promised land. The same will befall lawless Christians — they too will not be admitted into the kingdom of God. For *“without are dogs, and sorcerers, and whoremongers, and murderers, and idolaters, and whoever loves and makes a lie”* [Revelation 22:15]. And this is what the Lord says: *“Unless you repent, you shall all likewise perish”* [Luke 13:5].

sections.heading: The Ninevite Path: Fear, Repentance, Mercy

pairs.en: Sinners! Attend to this word and repent! Temporal destruction is fearful, but eternal destruction is far more fearful still. Let us, then, fear destruction, and repent, and escape it! The Ninevites feared the destruction that was to come upon them; they repented, and did not fall into destruction, but received mercy from our man-loving God. Let us too turn to our God with our whole heart, and repent, and cease provoking Him with our sins, that we also may receive mercy from Him. Amen.
